chunks: Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'What is your view regarding a man who struck a young woman on her belly, thereby injuring her womb and spoiling her menstruation?' And I mentioned that her menstruation had ceased due to that, whereas previously her menstruation had been regular. He (peace be upon him) said: 'She is awaited for a year; if her menstruation returns to what it was, [the matter is resolved], otherwise she is made to swear an oath, and the striker is fined one-third of her blood-money due to the spoiling of her womb and the cessation of her menstruation.'

key_terms.اسْتُحْلِفَتْ: she was made to swear an oath

ai.seo_question: What is the financial compensation (diyah) for a man who injures a woman's womb and stops her menstruation?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Kafi illustrates the Shia juristic approach to 'fasad al-rahim' (womb damage), distinguishing it from simple fractures by requiring a one-year observation period to determine if the injury is permanent. The imposition of one-third of the full blood-money (diyah) reflects the specific valuation of reproductive harm in classical fiqh, contingent upon the victim's oath to confirm the lasting nature of the dysfunction.

en.hubeali: Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Abu baseer who said,

‘I said to Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, ‘What is your<sup>asws</sup> view regarding a man who struck a woman upon her belly, so her womb was misplaced and it spoilt her menstruation’; and I mentioned, ‘It stopped her menstruation from her due to that, and her menstruations had been firm beforehand’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It would be awaited for her for a year, so if her menstruations were to come back to what they used to be, or else she would be made to wear an oath (for her state), and her attacker would be fined a third of the wergild due to spoiling her womb, and cutting off her menstruations’.
